meaning: to do something badly or skip necessary steps in order to save time or money
example: The builders cut corners, so the new bridge started to crack after one year.
origin: Possibly linked to walking across the corner of a path instead of following it all the way round, which saves time.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to turn sharply at a corner while driving
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This describes a physical movement, not the idiomatic meaning of doing a job badly to save time.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to work in a very careful and detailed way
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This is the opposite of the idiom, which describes skipping steps and lowering quality.
The idiom is about doing work badly or cheaply, not about making a lot of money fast.

explanation: 'Cut corners' means to do something badly or skip necessary steps in order to save time or money. It is often used about low-quality building, work or planning.
